Subject: Post-call: private connectivity playbook — SDK/auth, routing, VPC endpoints

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. This thread captures the short post-call recap, explicit asks, and proposed next steps so we can move the technical deep-dive to the right owners.

High-level context
- Use case: Atlas wants Redwood-hosted inference for customer-facing search and reranking; production traffic will include PII-derived queries and needs private connectivity from Atlas VPC (no public egress).
- Primary objectives: private connectivity (VPC endpoint or private link), strong auth with certificate-based options, minimal latency for embedding + reranker flows, and predictable egress controls for compliance.

Key points from call (short)
- SDK + Auth: Atlas will embed our SDK in server-side components. Primary auth preference: mTLS or customer-managed API gateway with client certs. Secondary: scoped API keys with IP allowlist for dev/test.
- Networking: prefer VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) + egress control — Atlas requires egress over corporate NAT with company DNS.
- DNS & Routing: Atlas wants canonical hostnames under redwood-internal.atlas.example, SRV/ALIAS records, and split-horizon DNS for internal name resolution.
- mTLS/cert rotation: Atlas asked about automated rotation and compatibility with internal CA infrastructure.
- Structured output/tool-calling & reranker: Atlas will send structured tool-calls and then a reranker pipeline (embeddings -> coarse filter -> rerank). Need latency targets (p95 < 250ms for rerank step).

Immediate asks (you asked us to respond in this thread)
1) A concise network requirements checklist (IP ranges, ports, DNS names, optional PrivateLink config).
2) A short diagram showing recommended topology for PrivateLink + SDK routing + egress.
3) Clarify mTLS support (client certs, rotation, HSM/KMS integration) and fallback options.
4) Proposed time for a technical deep-dive with our infra/PE teams (60–90 min).

Action items & next steps
- Priyom: attach a one-page connectivity checklist and public design notes (today).
- Nikhil: propose available times for the demo and include SRE/PE attendees (tomorrow).
- Atlas: confirm internal stakeholders for networking, compliance, and SRE; share a sanitized network diagram (if possible).

Subject: RE: Post-call: private connectivity playbook — SDK/auth, routing, VPC endpoints

Hi Katie — quick follow with the checklist and answers to your items. Sending the one-page checklist and a sample diagram as attachments. See inline answers below.

Attachments: redwood-private-connectivity-checklist.pdf (PDF, 210KB), atlas-network-diagram.png (PNG, 485KB)

Answers / recommendations
- PrivateLink: We support regional interface endpoints (recommended) and can optionally front with a global front door for multi-region failover. For strict low-latency workflows we recommend direct regional endpoints to avoid cross-region hops.
- Ports/protocols: Outbound from Atlas NAT to Redwood endpoints requires: TCP 443 (HTTPS) only. Additional internal ports used for health checks are over established TLS connections — no inbound open ports required.
- IP ranges: We publish a small stable set of egress IPs per region (will provide the CSV list in the checklist). We also support IP allowlist on a per-tenant basis.
- DNS: We can support split-horizon DNS. Option A (recommended): create private Route53 ALIAS to our PrivateLink endpoint DNS name. Option B: Atlas creates a CNAME to redwood-internal.{region}.redwood-inference.net and resolve via their resolver.
- mTLS / client certs: We support client certificate authentication for Private deployments and PrivateLink connections. Two modes: 1) Atlas presents client certs signed by an internal CA (we accept this; we just need the public CA chain to validate), or 2) use Redwood-managed certs with automated rotation and a customer-managed KMS/HSM for private key custody (enterprise plan). Rotation: we support automated cert rotation with rolling renewal; if Atlas uses their own CA for client certs, they are responsible for issuing and rotating — we provide a renewal webhook and a testing endpoint.
- Certificate validity & rotation cadence: We recommend 90-day certs for security teams; we support renewals with a 7-day pre-rotation validation window.
- Fallbacks: If mTLS is not doable for initial rollout, scoped API keys + IP allowlist + PrivateLink are acceptable for prod while we implement mTLS.

Structured output & reranker notes (short)
- SDK routing: The SDK can pin a model variant and route evaluation vs production traffic via headers; we support a route header to send cold-starts to a lower-cost instance.
- Embeddings & rerank latency: For a typical 3-stage flow (embedding -> candidate retrieve -> rerank), network hop to a regional PrivateLink endpoint adds ~5–10ms typical. Our measured p95 for rerank (single-node, 2k token context) in comparable customers is ~180–220ms; we will run a targeted benchmark during the demo with Atlas sample queries.

Next steps (operational)
- Sergio: coordinate with your calendar — propose 60–90 min slot PST next Tue/Wed morning.
- Atlas: if you can share a sanitized VPC/network diagram and primary region, we’ll prepare the deep-dive doc and a short perf runbook.

Cheers,

- Data residency: Yes — for Dedicated/Private plans we pin inference and embeddings to the customer region and isolate tenant data. No cross-region replication for ephemeral KV/embeddings unless configured for multi-region failover.
- MAP: See short owner list below (we'll attach a one-page MAP before the deep-dive):

  * Certs & Auth — Atlas secops (owner: Atlas) + Redwood security (owner: Nikhil) — lead time: 5–7 business days depending on CA handoff or Redwood-managed path.
  * Perf run & SLO signoff — Redwood PE (owner: Nikhil) + Atlas SRE (owner: TBD) — lead time: 2 business days to run baseline after topology is provisioned.
